q: Describe the causes of the industrial backwardness of Pakistan in detail, at the time of independence and mention the remedial steps taken by the government of Pakistan?
a: Answers: Causes of Industrial Backwardness of Pakistan There were only a few textiles and cement factories notable, at the time of independence, Agricultural raw material was also used by a few small factories e.g. cotton, jute, Nour, and oil-producing plants. We got only 34 poorly conditioned factories out of 921, of undivided India at partition. The industrial department of Pakistan was very poor and backward and the causes of the backwardness were as follows: (i) Industrial Policy of the British Government. The British Government, from the very beginning, adopted the policy of not establishing industries in Muslim majority areas of und vided India and leaving them in the fate of agriculture because the supply of raw material from these areas could remain to continue to English mills and factories. Had the industries been established in Muslim majority areas of undivided India, the English industries would have not progressed largely. Thus, due to British industrial policy, our country remained backward in industries. (ii) Lack of availability of Capital. Capital is said to be the running blood of industry as it holds the basic importance for the industrial development of a country. This facility is provided either by the private or public sectors. But, due to the backwardness of our industries, in 1947, the capitalists were shy to invest their capital. Moreover, there were no financial institutes to feed the industries, at that time. Thus, our industries remained progress less for many years.

q: Discuss the causes of the poor Banking System in Pakistan at the time of Independence?
a: Answers: 1. The backwardness of the Banking System The Commercial Banks of Pakistan were mostly owned by non-Muslims. Although the Muslims were, also traders and businessmen, they were handicapped by a lack of capital. The Hindus being more experienced; with more capital, dominated the trade, business, and banking of the country, They paid more attention to economic and financial organizations, being experts in accounts. They started transferring their capital to India, after the announcement of the 3rd June plan. The Banking system of Pakistan was disturbed badly. There were 631 scheduled Banks in the country, at the time of independence; but afterward, they began to close, due to a lack of capital. We had not any Central Bank and "The Reserve Bank of India" was entrusted with the duties of the Central Bank of Pakistan. This Bank took no interest in Pakistan's Economy and continued ignoring our financial benefits. Under such circumstances, the establishment of a central bank was badly needed in Pakistan. The Government made plans for it and established the Central Bank, namely, "The State Bank of Pakistan", inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah on the 1st of July, 1948. The Bank issued currency first time in October 1948. Afterward, a chain of banking organizations ran up continuously. The National Bank of Pakistan was established on the 8th of November, 1949. National and Grindlay's Bank and Bank of America were already working. Besides, Habib Bank Limited and Australasia Banks were also taking part in establishing our Banking System,

q: Write down the causes of agricultural backwardness in Pakistan?
a: What steps the government has taken to tackle this problem? Answer: Agriculture Backwardness in Pakistan At the time of independence, the country had a very poor economic setup. The people were the prey to poverty and misery. They, mostly, earned their living by agriculture but it was in a very backward position as the yield per acre was very low. The cultivators were living hand to mouth. Even the country being agricultural, faced the problem of food deficiency. The agricultural and their marketing conditions were quite unsatisfactory, we inherited the problems from the undivided Indian Govt. The causes which are mentioned below: (i) Land Tenure System. It was a defective land system. The greater part of cultivable land was the property of Landlords i.e. jageerdars and zamindars. Millions of farmers worked on these lands on very poor terms. Due to the unjust distribution of land, the farmers did not work zealously. One-fifth land of the total area of Punjab and 50% of cultivable land of N.W.F.P., was the property of landlords. According to the report of 1955, there were 8.6 million acres of agricultural land in Sind. Out of it, 1.1 million acres were owned by 124 jageerdars and 6 million acres of land were the property of only 3000 zamindars, who did not pay proper attention to their lands. Thus, one of the causes of our agricultural backwardness was the unjust and defective land tenure system. (ii) Lack of proper Irrigation System. At the time of Independence, immigration was done by means of wells and canals, while the "Barani lands" were left at the mercy of uncertain rainfall. The modern means of irrigation were not available then. Consequently, a large portion of agricultural land remained uncultivated. Thus, uncertain rainfall and lack of proper means of irrigation were also responsible for agricultural backwardness in our country.
